Subject: Initial redlines - MSA + Order Form (liability section)

Markus / Laura / Michael / Emily,

Attaching our initial redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. High level — Evelyn is asking for a one-way consequential damages exclusion (favoring you); customer counsel put in a broad carve-out to preserve certain indirect relief. Legal flagged three hot spots: (1) mutual vs one-way exclusion; (2) definition of "consequential/special/incidental" (they want to keep it very broad); and (3) damage cap carve-outs (IP indemnity, willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and data loss).

Quick asks:
- Laura: can you propose a clean fallback that keeps the exclusion mutual but limits the definition of consequential damages to truly indirect losses and preserves carve-outs for data breach and IP?
- Michael/Emily: if you can circulate a short note on why Evelyn needs a one-way exclusion, that will help speed resolution with procurement.

Attachments: EvelynCorp_MSA_Redline_20260212.pdf (redline), OrderForm_RFQ-011_20260212.xlsx (pricing + term sheet)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial redlines - MSA + Order Form (liability section)

Thanks Rohan — reviewed. I attached proposed language below (copied into the redline PDF) and a short rationale. Key points: 

1) Mutual exclusion — recommend mutual: a one-way exclusion creates asymmetric risk transfer and will materially affect run-rate economics for Redwood and the teams we rely on. Proposing the exclusion read: 

    "Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, indirect, exemplary or punitive damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement, except as expressly provided below."

2) Definition clarity — avoid an exhaustive list that expands indirect losses. My suggested definition for clarity (we included this in the redline): 

    "For purposes of this Section, 'consequential damages' means reasonably foreseeable indirect losses that arise from failure to meet stated performance metrics (for example, lost revenue directly attributable to downtime exceeding agreed SLOs), and does not include general loss of business or speculative future profits."

3) Carve-outs to the exclusion (these remain uncapped): IP infringement indemnity, willful misconduct or gross negligence, breach of confidentiality or data security obligations resulting in unauthorized access to Customer Data, and liability for taxes and third-party claims. We also propose a mutual liability cap set at the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $2,000,000.

I know sales will push to limit exceptions. If Procurement/Evelyn wants a one-way exclusion, ask them to explicitly limit the definition of "consequential" and keep the core carve-outs — otherwise we will need leadership sign-off on an asymmetric allocation.

Attachment: Proposed_Mutual_Liability_Language_snippet (in PDF)

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Laura et al,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Evelyn's position: we need a one-way exclusion **in favor of us** because we will be integrating Redwood outputs into our customer-facing product and want to limit exposure for indirect losses caused by downstream integrations. Our asks are practical: keep the exclusion one-way but narrow the term 'consequential' so it doesn't swallow the breach carve-outs. Proposed counter-language (excerpt):

    "Customer shall not be liable to Supplier for consequential, special, incidental, or punitive damages arising out of or related to Customer's use of the Services, provided that this exclusion shall not apply to (i) liability arising from Customer's indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims; (ii) willful misconduct or fraud; and (iii) damages resulting from Customer's breach of confidentiality obligations where such breach materially compromises Supplier's systems."

We understand Redwood's request for a mutual cap. Evelyn can accept a mutual monetary cap but expects the exclusion of indirect losses to remain one-way. As to the cap amount, Emily and procurement propose the greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $5,000,000.

We flagged this with our legal team and procurement — our goal is to land efficient wording that doesn't require C-suite escalation. If Redwood insists on mutual exclusion, please confirm the mutual exceptions will survive and that the definition won't allow recovery of speculative lost profits.

Attachment: Evelyn_Comments_Liability_20260215.docx

Best,
